summary.headline: Ashiana Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR107 crore (from INR293 crore) on delayed OCs; bookings INR358 crore, management guides FY27 presales INR2,200 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 bookings were INR358 crore across 234 units (3.6 lakh sq ft), moderating from a strong prior quarter, while collections rose 6% YoY to INR409 crore. Average realisation rose 37% YoY to INR9,923 per sq ft on product mix. Reported revenue fell to INR107 crore from INR293 crore, which management attributed to handover timing; two projects worth about INR532 crore of revenue received OCs in mid-July and so fall into Q2. Operating cash generation was INR121 crore, and the company acquired 28.55 acres at Vadgaon, Maval (Pune) for a Senior Living project with about 20 lakh sq ft saleable area and INR1,800 crore potential sales value.

segments.name: Senior Living
segments.commentary: Senior Living presales were about INR570 crore in FY26 from roughly INR100 crore five years ago; management targets about 25% CAGR and INR1,500 crore presales by FY29-30. Senior Living was about 23% of the business per management, vs 10% five years ago.

segments.name: Regular housing (Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi)
segments.commentary: Management flagged limited inventory to sell in these key markets, which it cited as a reason for a possible presales dip in the near term. Ashiana Nitara Phase 1 (Jaipur) handovers began in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target about INR2,200 crore; management says it is confident of holding it. Presales were INR859 crore as of 31 July 2026.
H1 FY27 presales exit expected at INR1,050-1,100 crore, then run-rate maintained.
FY27 reported revenue expected around INR2,000 crore per the investor deck (slide 15).
ROE: 15% is now the floor target on a long-term basis; management said FY27 ROE will reach about 20% and may stay above 20% for a few years.
Medium term: presales of INR3,000-4,000 crore needed to sustain ROE; Senior Living GDV target about INR10,000 crore as a first milestone.
Capex budget of about INR800 crore for FY27 for land/deals, including about INR180 crore deployed in Q1.
Dividend policy: most capital retained; management does not intend buybacks.
capex_capacity: Vadgaon, Maval (Pune): 28.55 acres, about 20 lakh sq ft saleable, about INR1,800-2,000 crore revenue underwritten at INR9,000-10,000 per sq ft; plan to sell about 2 lakh sq ft a year (about 10-year build, faster at 3 lakh sq ft a year). Launch expected in H2 of next financial year. NCD financing was provided by the landlords, with 25% of purchase value and a 6% revenue share.
Ashiana Oma launched in July 2026; Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) launch expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27 and is critical to reaching guidance.
Bengaluru (Kanakapura Road) Senior Living project: definitive documents pending; two people deployed to prepare launch; announcement expected soon.
Business development in advanced talks in Bengaluru; active talks in Jamshedpur (small deal expected soon), Chennai, Mumbai, Pune and NCR; further announcements targeted for Q3 FY27.
Senior Living: five projects already deployed, four with about 51 lakh sq ft in the pipeline plus Bengaluru. Land bank of 5 million sq ft is all Senior Living per management (slide 19).
demand_pricing: Management said residential demand softened in the quarter on global uncertainty and buyer wait-and-watch; prices remained resilient, and premiumisation continues.
Ashiana Oma launch in July 2026 drove July sales above the whole of Q1.
Management said units fell (407 to 234 YoY per analyst) partly from lower inventory in some markets, and partly the company's choice.

Gurugram resale in Ashiana Amarah: management said resale stock should be no more than about 20% of Phase 1, versus 80-90% trading for other Gurugram developers, because resale was not allowed without registry or possession.
Senior Living pricing is rising on ticket size and premium product mix; management cited higher marketing efficiency (Chennai Ashiana Shubham marketing cost down from about 8% to 4-5% of sales).

qa_highlights.question: Which launches will drive H2 bookings, and what supports the FY27 presales guidance after a soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July presales (Ashiana Oma launch) exceeded all of Q1, with full-year presales at about INR859 crore as of 31 July. H1 exit expected at INR1,050-1,100 crore; Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) in Q3 or Q4 is critical to the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable presales trajectory over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not targeting sustained near-term presales growth; a dip is possible this year or next, partly from low Gurugram and Jaipur/Bhiwadi inventory. Senior Living is targeted at about 25% CAGR, with INR1,500 crore presales by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% vs 20% ROE messaging consistent, and can ROE exceed 20% on a reported basis?
qa_highlights.answer: 15% is now the floor ROE target on a long-term basis; management agreed FY27 could reach about 20% and may stay above 20% for a few years. Sustaining ROE needs medium-term presales of INR3,000-4,000 crore and earnings growth, with capital not being distributed.

qa_highlights.question: What project-level margin structure underpins the ROE target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 30% project gross margin, 12% SG&A, 18% PBT and 12-13% PAT margin; sustaining this gives ROE in the teens, and margin improvement could take it to about 20%. Levers cited were Senior Living pricing per sq ft, premiumisation and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 revenue drop a timing issue, and what is the FY27 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Two projects, Ashiana Anmol Phase 3 and Ashiana Amarah Phase 1, worth about INR532 crore of revenue got OCs in mid-July and move into Q2. FY27 reported revenue is expected at about INR2,000 crore per slide 15; management asked investors to judge on a YoY basis.

qa_highlights.question: Did units fall from 407 to 234 deliberately or due to a volume slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was hard to call it not deliberate, citing lower inventory in some markets. It pointed to the July Ashiana Oma launch and the INR2,200 crore full-year presales guidance as the basis for being on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vadgaon, Pune underwriting, absorption and NCD structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Underwriting assumes INR9,000-10,000 per sq ft on about 20 lakh sq ft, or INR1,800-2,000 crore; sales of about 2 lakh sq ft a year over about 10 years, or 3 lakh sq ft a year in a faster case. Landlords provided the NCD financing with 25% of purchase value and a 6% revenue share; launch expected in H2 of next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IFC partnerships and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No active agreement with IFC; the second platform deployed only about INR100 crore into Aaroham before its timeline lapsed, as ticket-size caps blocked other projects. FY27 capex budget is about INR800 crore, including about INR180 crore deployed in Q1, covering active deals.

risks_watch: Revenue timing: about INR532 crore of Q2 revenue depends on OC timing (Anmol Phase 3, Amarah Phase 1); Q2 reported revenue may be lumpy again.
FY27 presales guidance of INR2,200 crore requires H1 exit at INR1,050-1,100 crore and Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 launch in Q3/Q4; slippage would hit guidance.
Limited inventory in Gurugram, Jaipur and Bhiwadi may cause a presales dip in the near term; Senior Living must scale to offset.
Margin compression on Anmol and Amarah: management guided blended gross margin in the mid-20s, below the 30% project-level target.
Bengaluru (Kanakapura Road) Senior Living definitive documents still pending; other BD deals (Jamshedpur, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, NCR) targeted for Q3 FY27.
key_quotes: I think INR2,200 crores is what we are targeting.
So, reported revenues in Slide 15 of the deck, we have given an indication of how much we expect to report this year.
So run rate will be maintained from there on.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on FY27 presales (INR2,200 crore) and ROE, but cautious on near-term volumes, citing softer demand and low inventory in key markets. It was evasive on the 15% vs 20% ROE question and on unit decline (407 to 234), and it steered investors to slide 15 and annual rather than quarterly revenue.

growth.why: FY27 presales target INR2,200 crore held and FY27 revenue ~INR2,000 crore guided, with H1 presales exit INR1,050-1,100 crore; backing is partly specific (INR859 crore presales to 31 July, Ashiana Oma launched July, INR532 crore OCs moving into Q2) but Aaroham Phase 3 and Senior Living pipeline timing are not yet firm, and management flagged a possible presales dip.
